bet.text: A massive hopper for cycling plus massive shooting throughput gives a higher effective rate than most turrets, even those that shoot all match.

demand.text: An early target was to score 360 fuel without relying on partners, expecting defense.
The team first favored the bump partly to ease a level 3 climb, then judged level 3 not worth the effort.
The team page lists efficient fuel scoring, a level 1 climb and strong autonomous routines.

auto.text: In a mic'd-up match a voice that reads as 1678's plans a double sweep from the left trench.
At Half Moon Bay a commentator describes the robot crossing the center at a slant so its bumper corner piled up fuel for the way back, then looping close to its own hub, where scored fuel falls.

cycle.text: In a mic'd-up match a voice that reads as 1678's describes going out by the trench and back over the bump.
The load is fired once readiness checks pass.
In a Sacramento qualification match without defense, a commentator describes 1678 passing fuel to a turret partner between active shifts, then dumping its own load and collecting from the middle.

endgame.text: The level 1 climber is the lift that carries the top of the hopper, and it can climb at either side of the tower or straight down the middle.
A commentator calls its Sacramento climb very fast and worth more than fuel in the last few seconds.

fallback.text: A poster notes the driver can lower the hopper, hold fewer balls and use the trench if the bump is blocked.
Team 2481 says the two robots screened for each other against defense, especially in the division finals, though it still slowed cycles by a few seconds.
Two spare intakes travel with the team.

gave_up.text: Early tradeoff slides, which left the choice open, describe a level 3 climber as heavy, big and slow; the robot climbs level 1.
Robot weight became a bigger and bigger issue during the season and forced cuts.

changed.text: The first architecture was replaced early.
Merging the level 1 climb with the hopper dates to day 15.

The Sacramento robot's wooden tunnel backer and two side cameras were later removed, and grip tape replaced silicone on the drum. Sources differ on the drum (steel at Sacramento, aluminum on the team page) and hood rollers (two, three).
The one major CAN failure in competition came in the last Einstein match.

outcome.text: 61-9-0 in official play; won the Milstein division; captain of the Milstein alliance on Einstein; ranked 17 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 290.57, Milstein).

solves.text: Leave room for the ball path, stay agile and cross the bump smoothly

facts.text: 27 in by 27 in with SDS MK5n modules, chosen to leave the most space for the ball path
1/16 in pocketed belly pan; the roller floor pivots up for access to battery and electronics
Plastic strips brace each side underneath so it goes smoothly over the bump
Drive rails went from 1/8 in wall to 1/16 in to save weight; the side tubes were later swapped for 0.090 in ones with a narrower climber sprocket slot

cost.text: The 1/16 in rails bent slightly after repeated impacts, mostly at the climber sprocket slots

solves.text: Get balls into the robot fast while taking crashes without driver worry

facts.text: 2 in silicone-covered carbon-fiber roller with a 1.25 in carbon-fiber kicker bar
Two Kraken X60s drive the roller; one X60 deploys the intake through a compact MAXSpline gearbox
1/8 in thick 2 in by 1 in aluminum crash bar, with hot-swappable SRPP plates
Two sleeved hex shafts guide balls and keep them off the main roller after pickup
At Sacramento, four bolts per side held the intake to its wrist plates
Intake wrist plates are 7075 aluminum, 0.25 in thick for impacts and 0.5 in where they meet the hard stop
Two nut strips on the front rail hold the pivot gearbox without trouble, since it is isolated from most large forces
A commenter who asked at an event says the compression was slightly modified from one 6328 published

cost.text: After the first event the team found the hopper and intake especially broke down in midfield collisions, and focused on robustness
In a mic'd-up match a voice that reads as 1678's warns that hard hits can kill the intake, and a voice afterwards says a carbon-fiber pop-up bar snapped
The SplineXL in the pivot wore and added backlash, more than chain stretch did; crush blocks under the sprocket and wrist plates were added later in the season

functions.name: Expanding hopper

solves.text: Carry a large load and still go under the trench

functions.type: hopper that extends with the intake and with the climber

facts.text: About 75 to 80 balls when expanded
Horizontal part: 1/8 in polycarbonate sides and corrugated plastic front, moved by the intake
Upper part: two 0.75 in square tubes on the climber carry a corrugated plastic top
A #25 chain and one X60 move the upper part up and down
Bumper-mounted polycarbonate walls support the hopper
A narrator calls it the first robot to use the trench and still hold so many balls
The vertical extension is 0.75 x 1.5 in tube inside 1 x 2 in tube
The chain links to both sides of a block fixed to the tube with three #10-32 bolts

cost.text: Broke down in collisions at the first event along with the intake

solves.text: Accelerate a full hopper to the shooter while one ball wins the race into the tunnel

facts.text: Five 1 in dead-axle rollers and three 2 in flex-wheel rollers
Rollers near the intake tilt little; the three flex-wheel rollers sit much steeper to minimize keystoning; the last two dead-axle rollers follow the ball's path through the feeder
One X60 drives it, at 3:1 for the 2 in rollers and 1.5:1 for the 1 in rollers
Carbon-fiber tubes covered in silicone on small dead-axle stubs
A pin through the plate and hard stop holds it down in a match
A smaller inner diameter, for more material, with Onyx and 6 to 8 walls made the stubs very durable

cost.text: The roboRIO's USB port sits under the pivot and was difficult to reach
Printed roller stubs sheared under load in PA6-CF with 6 to 8 walls, and occasionally in Onyx; printing at 45 degrees helped but lowered print quality

functions.name: Ball tunnel and feeder

solves.text: Accelerate balls consistently before they reach the drum

functions.type: accelerating roller tunnel with a separate feeder roller

facts.text: Brings balls to about this share of shot speed
Two X60s; the backing was a wooden plank at Sacramento, added to raise compression and remove dead spots, and became 1.25 in dead-axle rollers
The 2 in feeder roller has its own X60, so the tunnel can spin up before feeding
J shape, after an earlier S shape
The shooter version that replaced the wooden backer cut compression from 0.7 to 0.35 in, removed the dead spots and helped shot consistency moderately

functions.name: Shooter

solves.text: Launch a whole hopper rapidly and accurately into the hub

functions.type: full-width drum shooter with adjustable hood

facts.text: Side plates of 3/16 in aluminum, 25 in apart
Drum differs by source: the Sacramento interview says steel tubing with aluminum end plugs, about 6 lb; the team page says 3.5 in aluminum covered in skateboard grip tape
Hood rollers are driven from the drum: two in the interview, three on the team page
Four X60s power drum and hood rollers so it can ferry from the opponent zone
An X44 moves the hood through a jackshaft for a wide range of angles
Time from trigger press to shooting at Sacramento, about
Hood plates turn between two Delrin bushings screwed to the shooter plates
A commenter after week 1 says it seemed to empty the hopper in under 2 seconds when not aiming into the goal

cost.text: From the reveal video, a poster estimates about 20 to 25 percent of shots missed, and sees that as the drawback of high-volume fixed shooters; another answers that misses do not matter when the target is not the hub
Drum silicone expanded at higher speeds, and the team had to develop methods against it
A commenter says small aiming errors far away make an outer lane of a wide stream miss, so it generally needs close shots

functions.name: Climber

solves.text: Combine the climb with a hopper that can shrink to go under the trench

functions.type: level 1 climber built into the hopper

facts.text: Grips the tower with material left from the previous year
Reaches level 1
The hopper's upper part is attached to it and moves by #25 chain and one X60

solves.text: Get enough vision updates to localize for almost all of the match

facts.text: A Limelight plus two side cameras at the Sacramento event; later one Limelight 4 on the back face
Two CANranges, in the hopper and the shooter
The side cameras were cut to save weight because, as placed and used, they were not really helping
Changing vision standard deviations while shooting forced faster convergence
Odometry was good enough after a block in auto to reach a tag and relocalize
The side cameras were meant to speed convergence before shots, see tags along the midline in auto and improve pose when ferrying from far away; a softer ferry made the last one unimportant

cost.text: The side Arducams on PhotonVision had frozen streams, and an Orange Pi that stopped updating after crossing the bump

solves.text: Fire only when the whole stream will have consistent energy and a clear path

facts.text: Checks include robot tilt, whether the shot would be blocked, drum and tunnel speed, and hood position
LEDs are red until the criteria are met, then yellow and blue while shooting
An Elastic dashboard shows time left in a shift, adjusted for who won auto
One driver; software handles shot alignment and targeting

decisions.choice: Wide drum shooter with a large hopper
decisions.because: widening the shooter prototype and adding a massive ramp gave far more throughput
decisions.instead_of: the different architecture first being designed

decisions.choice: Dumper that fits under the trench
decisions.because: merging the level 1 climb with the hopper gave the capacity while still going under
decisions.instead_of: the bump, favored right after kickoff because of the first blockading rule wording and an easier level 3 climb

decisions.because: early tradeoff slides, which left the choice open, call it quick, simple and reliable, and say a faster shooting rate favors it
decisions.instead_of: a level 3 climb, described as heavy, big and slow

decisions.choice: One active intake roller with a fixed kicker bar
decisions.because: two active rollers on Alpha and Beta were not working

decisions.choice: Aluminum crash bar in front of the intake
decisions.because: it takes impacts, so the roller can be carbon fiber, which usually shatters
the S shape changed ball speed so balls deflected off the drum and shots were inconsistent

decisions.choice: CAN loop with few solder joints or connectors
decisions.because: fewer breaks reduce possible failures, and service loops make a break at a component easy to fix

decisions.choice: Crimp CAN ring terminals only once (advice after the season)
decisions.because: the motor terminals whose CAN wire snapped at the base had all been crimped twice; a team member blames bad crimping and vibration

decisions.choice: Main breaker at the back of the robot
decisions.because: 2 AWG wire could hardly make the bends beside the battery, and the back is far more accessible
decisions.cost: a longer wire than ideal, with extra resistance the team calls negligible, though it took almost the same amount of wire as the looped route

decisions.because: it stands up to repeated impacts, is thin, bends enough to fit over the robot, and takes rivets for hopper walls and nut flanges
an X44, tried early in the season, often overheated
full automation had too many edge cases and fully manual control gave the driver too much to watch; one button expands and one runs the whole contraction with the intake
decisions.instead_of: a fully automatic or fully manual hopper, both tried

decisions.choice: Skateboard grip tape on the drum
decisions.because: it is easier to maintain and keeps its grip much longer, and other teams such as 1114 did well with it; cat tongue was not tried
a reply in the team's release thread says pure pursuit drew its own arcs and had no quick path editor, so tuning meant guess and rerun; Choreo gave fine control and quick iteration
decisions.instead_of: a custom point-to-point system on pure pursuit, tried early in the season
